metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent tried to create two column bar charts for 2019 and 2020 monthly costs. During the reliable prefix, it correctly scanned the month and total cost data in column I (Jan=399, Feb=404, Mar=429, ...).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can scan spreadsheet rows, identify max values by visual inspection, navigate cells, and type text values
metadata.failure_analysis: Failed at step 3 due to column I header confusion. The reliable prefix (steps 0-2) showed the agent correctly read the per-month layout and all monthly values.
metadata.task_rationale: Targets the data-scanning capability from steps 0-2. March 2019 (row 5) has the highest monthly total at 429, above other months. The model needs to scan column I rows 3-14 and identify the peak month.
metadata.explanation: The 2019 monthly totals in column I (rows 3-14) are: Jan=399, Feb=404, Mar=429, Apr=399, May=389, Jun=419, Jul=419, Aug=364, Sep=359, Oct=364, Nov=374, Dec=389. March (429) is the highest. Cell K2 must contain 'Mar'. Initial state is empty so test passes only after correct entry. [Fixed: renamed getter/metric function suffixes from 8-char '86c23ec8' to proper 32-char MD5 'd4b207925bd2d0c3ababe1e319fa8b1f' computed from task_stem|variation_index]

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cell K2 from sheet index 0 of the xlsx file using openpyxl, which matches the evaluator config.
Metric performs case-insensitive string comparison with expected value 'Mar', so 'Mar', 'mar', 'MAR' all pass — appropriate for abbreviated month names.
Expected value 'Mar' is correctly grounded: task rationale confirms March 2019 has the highest monthly total (429) across all 12 months.
Negative control is satisfied: empty K2 returns None, causing metric to return 0.0, so the initial state correctly fails.
Actual getter and metric function files use the correct 32-char MD5 suffix ('d4b207925bd2d0c3ababe1e319fa8b1f'), matching the evaluator.func and result.type fields in the task JSON.
